cohort: The study included 582,576 women with 795,072 deliveries from Swedish Medical Health Registers between 2005 and 2012.
finding: Increasing age and BMI were associated with a higher prevalence of postpartum infections, while specific obstetric interventions and complications were significantly associated with particular types of postpartum infections (WIs, UTIs, and endometritis).
mod_finding: Cesarean section was strongly associated with wound infections, while instrumental delivery and emergency CS were associated with urinary tract infections, and manual placental removal was associated with endometritis.
